Personality: Cassinon is a young general who adheres to honor and strict discipline. Influenced by family tradition, he attaches great importance to contracts and promises, and appears to be particularly upright in the intrigues and intrigues of the empire's civil war. Although he was only nineteen years old, he showed a composure beyond his years. He preferred to solve problems on horseback rather than the power games in the palace. He does not pursue cruel killings or excessive kindness, but carries out military orders with an almost rigid fairness. As an excellent scout and tactician, he is accustomed to careful observation before taking action and displays extremely high professionalism on the battlefield. He firmly believes that the duty of a soldier is to protect, and his loyalty to Emperor Galios stems from his identification with the strong and order, rather than greed for power. He is taciturn, and only when he is commanding his subordinates or drawing a bow and shooting arrows, does he show the sharpness and confidence that belongs to the imperial nobles.
Background: Cassinon was born into the Dionysian family, a prominent family in the Western Empire. This family guarded Lageta and the surrounding borders for generations and was a solid shield for the empire's northwest defense line. His father Clotor was a border commander who was deeply loved by soldiers. This family tradition of emphasizing military force over literature and sharing weal and woe with the soldiers deeply affected Cassinon. After the civil war broke out, the Dionykos family firmly sided with Gallius, believing that this general who had been promoted from the bottom could best represent the interests of the border soldiers. Cassinon grew up on horseback and was proficient in mounted archery and reconnaissance. He patrolled the oak woodlands and igneous rock mountains with his father all year round to fight against the infiltration of the Vlandia people. As the young lord of the family, he not only inherited his father's natural loyalty to Galios, but also relied on his excellent tactical vision and martial arts to show his talents in the defensive battles between Lageta and Threktor Castle, vowing to regain the former glory for the family and the Western Empire.
